TELECOM CUSTOMER CHURN — END-TO-END ANALYSIS

1,869 customers
already left. 1,587 more are showing the same signal.

A full pipeline built on 7,043 telecom customer records — cleaned, explored, modeled with XGBoost across five tuning strategies, and scored for who's leaving next. Every number on this page comes out of that pipeline.

00 — ARCHITECTURE

Six files, one straight line

No orchestration framework — a deliberate, ordered handoff between five notebooks and a Power BI report, each one reading the last one's output.

01
Customer-Churn.csv
Raw source
7,043 rows, 21 columns. IBM's public telecom sample — demographics, subscribed services, contract terms, billing.
02
Analysis_EDA.ipynb
Clean & explore
TotalCharges coerced to numeric, 11 nulls dropped, tenure binned into 6 groups. Univariate and bivariate passes against Churn.
03
ML_Model_Building.ipynb
Model & tune
Decision Tree baseline → SMOTEENN → XGBoost → RandomizedSearchCV → Optuna. Seven algorithms compared, two saved as .pkl.
04
AI_Analyst.ipynb
Score & narrate
Loads both saved models, scores every customer, assigns High/Medium/Low risk, and generates plain-language findings automatically.
05
churn_predictions.csv
Scored output
7,032 customers × probability + risk band, from both the XGBoost and Optuna-tuned models, side by side.
06
Project1_reports.pbix
Report & dashboard
Three report pages plus a published dashboard, built directly on the scored file. Sections below.
01 — DATA EXPLORATION

What the data said before any model touched it

Univariate and bivariate analysis across every column, correlated against the Churn flag.

TARGET DISTRIBUTION — n = 7,043
5,174 stayed
1,869 left
73.4% retained26.6% churned
CHURN RATE BY SEGMENT, VS. 26.58% BASELINE
Month-to-month contract vs. one/two-year terms
42.71%
No online security add-on of customers without the service
41.78%
No tech support add-on of customers without the service
41.65%
Higher monthly charge, lower tenure, and lower total charge move together — and all three point toward high churn. Total Charges looking "protective" on its own is misleading once tenure is accounted for. — insight recorded directly in Analysis_EDA.ipynb
2.78× non-churn to churn class imbalance in the training split — the reason every later modeling decision routes through resampling or class weights
HOLDS UP ACROSS THE DATA
  • Electronic check payers churn most among the four payment methods
  • Fiber optic internet correlates with higher churn than DSL
  • Customers 5+ years in show the lowest churn of any tenure band
  • Gender, phone service, and multiple-lines status: near zero effect
  • Non-senior citizens churn at a higher rate than senior citizens
02 — MODEL BUILDING

Two tuned XGBoost runs made the cut

A plain Decision Tree, three resampling strategies, and seven algorithms were run before landing here. Both saved models are used side by side in scoring.

best_xgboost_churn_model.pkl
XGBoost · RandomizedSearchCV
0.72ACCURACY
0.75CHURN RECALL
0.58CHURN F1
50 iterations, 5-fold CV, scored on F1. Best params landed at max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.1, scale_pos_weight ≈2.74 — tuned specifically to catch churners, not just be "accurate."
best_optuna_churn_model.pkl HIGHER CV F1
XGBoost · Optuna search
0.73ACCURACY
0.75CHURN RECALL
0.59CHURN F1
Bayesian search over 9 hyperparameters incl. L1/L2 regularization. CV F1 of 0.625 vs. 0.620 for the randomized search — a narrow win, which is why both models ship to scoring rather than one being discarded.
BASE DECISION TREE 0.55 F1 + SMOTEENN 0.60 F1 RANDOM FOREST + SMOTEENN 0.63 F1 XGB + scale_pos_weight 0.63 F1 CATBOOST 0.63 F1

03 — AI ANALYST OUTPUT

Every customer, sorted into a verdict

AI_Analyst.ipynb runs both saved models against all 7,032 customers, bands each one by predicted probability, and writes the recommendations below without a human touching the wording.

1,587
22.6% of the base · probability ≥ 0.70
High risk
Of these, 1,078 have already churned in the historical record — the model is finding real signal, not noise. The rest are the priority retention list.
1,878
26.7% of the base · probability 0.40–0.69
Medium risk
A mixed group — worth a lighter-touch nudge (support outreach, add-on offer) rather than a full retention campaign.
3,567
50.7% of the base · probability < 0.40
Low risk
Stable base. 3,372 of these customers have, in fact, stayed — the model's confidence here is well placed.
AUTO-GENERATED RECOMMENDATIONS — AI_Analyst.ipynb, final cell
  • Offer incentives to move month-to-month customers onto longer-term contracts
  • Promote Online Security to customers who don't currently have it
  • Offer Tech Support packages to customers currently without one
  • Prioritize the XGBoost high-risk list for retention campaigns
  • Use the Optuna high-risk list to cross-check targeting
